title: agents tests install the AppArmor profile into the host's real /etc/apparmor.d through sudo
body:
## What happened (kovacs, 25 Oct 2026; Molt release-candidate Linux check at d15b82d, run by kovacs-sysadm)

Every one of agents.bats' 30 failures on kovacs prints `install: cannot remove '/etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict': Operation not permitted`, then `agents: sandbox profile: sudo could not install /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict`. The tests' sandbox-profile step aims at the host's real `/etc/apparmor.d`, through sudo. It failed on kovacs only because the test's sudo did not get root. kovacs-sysadm checked afterwards: the real profile and its `.molt-orig` and `.molt-rendered` copies are unchanged (mtime 2026-10-22T16:24:02), and journald holds no sudo entries in the window.

The cause: `molt_apparmor_dir` (lib/molt.sh) echoes `/etc/apparmor.d` with no override, and `lib/agent.sh` builds the installed profile's path from it. The managed-settings floor is redirected into the test root, but the AppArmor profile is not. On a Linux host where sudo needs no password, a test run overwrites the host's profile and `molt_apparmor_load` loads it into the kernel (`sudo apparmor_parser -r`). It passes on macOS because the sandbox-profile step is Linux only.

## Spec (vc, 25 Oct 2026)

- `molt_apparmor_dir` takes its directory from one override variable, the same way the managed-settings floor's root does, defaulting to `/etc/apparmor.d`. That one function stays the only place the path is named.
- test_helper points the override at the test root for every test, before any file's own setup runs, as it does for the agents root.
- No test reaches the real sudo or the real `apparmor_parser`. test_helper puts stubs first on PATH that record their argv and do nothing, the same as the launchctl stub from 0059. A test that exercises sudo or the parser fakes its own in front.
- A tripwire: a test run on Linux leaves `/etc/apparmor.d` unchanged. It is asserted from outside the suite, in the judge, by comparing mtimes before and after. It is not a test that touches /etc.
- Each new test is red with the change reverted. The full suite runs under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash, and on kovacs through kovacs-sysadm, with agents.bats green.


## As built (cc, 25 Oct 2026; merged by vc as f20383b)

- `molt_apparmor_dir` (lib/molt.sh) echoes `${MOLT_APPARMOR_DIR:-/etc/apparmor.d}` and is still the only place the path is named. `molt_claude_managed_dir` takes `MOLT_CLAUDE_MANAGED_DIR` first, then falls back to the platform default as before. The same hazard was there: until now only an `eval` in two test files moved it, and that never reached a `bin/molt` subprocess.
- test_helper exports both variables at file scope, into the run's temp dir, so they are set before any file's own setup runs and reach every subprocess. setup then points them into each test's own dir. The managed-dir `eval`s in agents.bats and molt.bats are gone, and `install_fake_apparmor` uses the variable.
- test_helper puts stubs for launchctl, sudo and apparmor_parser first on PATH, in one loop. Each stub records its argv to `calls.log` and does nothing.
- agents.bats has three new tests. One checks the sandbox profile resolves into the test's dir, in this shell, in a fresh bash, and as `/etc/apparmor.d` when the variable is unset. One checks the managed floor the same way, with the platform default when the variable is unset. One checks that `command -v` finds the stubs for sudo and apparmor_parser and that the stubs install nothing. Each was red with lib/molt.sh or test_helper reverted.
- The desk run at f24c2f1 (25 Oct 17:39-17:59Z) was green under Homebrew bash and /bin/bash. The PATH tripwire for launchctl, sudo and apparmor_parser recorded nothing, shellcheck -S warning was clean, and the shell critic was clean on lib/molt.sh and test_helper. It asked nothing of agents.bats, so that file has no critic coverage. Every liberator target under the real HOME was byte-identical before and after the run. vc's release-candidate run on the merge with 0063 and 0064 (bb7d32f) was green as well, and main's tree at f20383b is byte-identical to the tree that run tested.
- Still owed: the spec's Linux leg. That is the full suite on kovacs through kovacs-sysadm with agents.bats green, and `/etc/apparmor.d`'s mtimes unchanged across the run. It rides the Molt release-candidate re-run on kovacs.
